---
title: "ROSMAP"
description: "Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project: aging cohorts with brain donation, with clinical, neuropathology, and omics data. Controlled access through Synapse."
---

ROSMAP combines two longitudinal cohort studies run by the Rush Alzheimer's
Disease Center (RADC) in Chicago. The Religious Orders Study (ROS) enrolls
older Catholic nuns, priests, and brothers from across the US. The Rush Memory
and Aging Project (MAP) enrolls older adults from the Chicago area.
Participants enroll without dementia, have annual clinical evaluations, and
agree to donate their brain at death. The two studies share protocols, so
they're usually analyzed together.

- **Data:** the [AD Knowledge Portal](https://adknowledgeportal.synapse.org/)
  on Synapse. The ROSMAP study page is
  [syn3219045](https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn3219045).
- **Access:** controlled, through Synapse. Tomás adds lab members.

## What's in it

- Clinical and cognitive data from the annual visits
- Neuropathology from brain autopsy
- Omics, mostly from brain tissue: genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic (bulk
  and single-nucleus), proteomic, and metabolomic data

## Getting access

Access is given through Synapse. Tomás has ROSMAP access and can add students
and researchers. **If you need ROSMAP data and Tomás hasn't added you yet,
contact Tomás.** You'll need your own [Synapse](https://www.synapse.org)
account to be added, so create one first and send Tomás your username.

## Downloading

You can download files from the Synapse website, or with the Synapse
[Python client](https://python-docs.synapse.org/) (`synapseclient`) for
anything more than a few files. Log in with a personal access token, and keep
the token out of your code and out of Git.

## Publishing with ROSMAP data

The data use terms you accept on Synapse say how to cite and acknowledge the
data. Check them before you submit a manuscript.
